name: American hot-rod lead (SLO-style)
notes: Late-80s American hot-rod lead style: thick, singing, mid-rich high gain with a smooth top. Like the modern high gain preset in layout but with more mids, bigger coupling caps (less bass cut between stages), and a 6L6-family power amp with presence and depth (resonance) in the feedback loop. FROM SCHEMATICS (fairly sure): cascaded 12AX7 stages with a cold clipper, cathode follower, passive tone stack after the preamp, 6L6-family power tubes, presence and depth controls in the feedback loop. UNSURE / APPROXIMATED: all cathode and bias values, the bright cap, the high-passes between stages (80 and 120 Hz), tone stack values (british-style values with a 47k slope resistor and 250k treble pot), feedback amount (set for about 6 dB), depth as a -6 dB low shelf at 100 Hz in the feedback path. Phase inverter as one triode that gets half the input (each triode of the real long-tailed pair sees half the signal, so it has twice the headroom of a single stage). POWER SUPPLY: silicon rectifier and a big filter capacitor: a stiff, tight supply, as 60 ohm into 100 uF (supply_ohms, supply_uf on the power block), so the sag comes from the current the power tubes really draw. These two values are GUESSES from typical parts, not from this amp's schematic. (It replaced a sag block.) COUPLING: every coupling capacitor and the output transformer's low end are 1st-order high-passes (highpass1), as in the real circuit; each gain stage ends with its coupling capacitor into the next grid resistor (coupling_nf, grid_ohms; default 22 nF into 1 Mohm = 7.2 Hz). The cathode follower is DC-coupled to v2b's plate and drives the tone stack directly (coupling_nf 0 on both): the DC shift of hard clipping moves the cathode follower's working point, and the tone stack's capacitors block it. PREAMP SUPPLY: every gain stage (v1a, v1b, v2a_cold, v2b, cathode_follower, pi) hangs on the same supply through decoupling filters (preamp_targets), so it sags too, about 100 ms behind (preamp_filter_ms: a GUESS; real amps have 10k-ish resistors and 10-50 uF capacitors per node). OUTPUT TRANSFORMER: the core of a 100 W amp's transformer, saturating on full-power notes below about 30 Hz (transformer_sat_hz: a GUESS from the amp's size, not measured): loud low notes lose bass and get odd harmonics. POWER TUBES: four (pairs 2) into half the load (2100 ohm), as in the 100 W originals: each tube works as in one pair, so the clipping is the same; the supply feeds twice the current, so it sags more (the supply values were guessed for one pair and are still GUESSES).
